title: FDA enforcement discretion on Medication Guides for drugs dispensed to a health care professional for administration
subtopic: Medication Guides in inpatient and administration settings, and Medication Guides within a REMS
rule_summary: FDA's final guidance Medication Guides — Distribution Requirements and Inclusion in Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) (November 2011), which contains nonbinding recommendations, states that a Medication Guide need not be provided, meaning FDA intends to exercise enforcement discretion concerning its distribution to a patient, when a drug is dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration to a patient in an inpatient setting, or in an outpatient setting such as a clinic or dialysis or infusion center, except in listed circumstances. In those listed circumstances a Medication Guide must be provided to the patient or the patient's agent and FDA does not intend to exercise enforcement discretion: when the patient or the patient's agent requests a Medication Guide; when a drug is dispensed in an outpatient setting (for example a retail pharmacy or hospital ambulatory care pharmacy) and the product will then be used by the patient without direct supervision by a healthcare professional; the first time a drug is dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration to a patient in an outpatient setting; the first time a drug is dispensed in an outpatient setting of any kind after a Medication Guide is materially changed; and, when a drug is subject to a REMS that includes specific requirements for reviewing or providing a Medication Guide as part of an element to assure safe use, in accordance with the terms of the REMS. The guidance's Table 1 shows that where a drug is dispensed directly to the patient or caregiver in an outpatient setting (for example a retail pharmacy, a hospital ambulatory pharmacy or patient samples) the Medication Guide must be provided each time the drug is dispensed, while in an inpatient setting and where the drug is dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration in an outpatient setting FDA intends to exercise enforcement discretion as to providing it each time. The same guidance states that while all Medication Guides must meet the standard and requirements in Part 208, not every newly required Medication Guide will be an element of a REMS; that FDA may approve a Medication Guide under Part 208 without requiring a REMS when that alone is adequate; and that in most cases FDA expects to include a Medication Guide as part of a REMS only when the REMS includes elements to assure safe use.
exam_relevance: Separates the regulation from FDA's statement of enforcement policy, and shows that a request by the patient or the patient's agent defeats the enforcement discretion in every setting.

authority.name: FDA Guidance: Medication Guides — Distribution Requirements and Inclusion in Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS), November 2011
authority.section: Section III.A (Distribution of Medication Guides in Certain Settings), Table 1, and Section III.B.1 (Policy)

exceptions: Enforcement discretion does not extend to a case in which the patient or the patient's agent requests a Medication Guide.

Where a REMS includes specific requirements for reviewing or providing a Medication Guide as part of an element to assure safe use, the Medication Guide is provided in accordance with the terms of the REMS.
common_confusions: Treating FDA's enforcement discretion as an exemption written into 21 CFR Part 208; the guidance contains nonbinding recommendations describing when FDA intends to exercise enforcement discretion.
Carrying the inpatient approach to a retail pharmacy; where a drug is dispensed directly to the patient or caregiver the guidance expects a Medication Guide each time the drug is dispensed.

Assuming no Medication Guide is ever expected for a drug administered in a clinic or infusion center; the guidance expects one the first time the drug is dispensed there, after a material change, and whenever the patient or the patient's agent requests it.
Assuming every Medication Guide is part of a REMS; the guidance states that FDA may approve a Medication Guide under Part 208 without requiring a REMS.
verification_notes: Read the guidance PDF (12 pages) and its FDA landing page on 2026-09-14. FDA's guidance search lists the document as final guidance issued 11/18/2011 by CDER and CBER; the landing page states that it addresses when FDA intends to exercise enforcement discretion for a drug dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration to a patient and when a Medication Guide will be required as part of a REMS.
